text:
alex_chiang: heads-up — saw a sharp latency cliff on 8x-GPU TP all-reduce during long-context runs, looks message-size dependent. filing here before I run more sweeps

samir: which cluster / config? repro script? :eyes:

alex_chiang: prod-sim (8xA100-40G), fp16, seq_len=1024, batch=1 per replica. repro script attached in thread (short). key observation: throughput drops ~30% when per-rank payload hits ~48KB-64KB and again at ~512KB. traces point to all-reduce stalls, not compute.

rita_khan: can you paste the NCCL op breakdown? ring vs tree times?

alex_chiang: pasted below — this is a condensed scrape from nsys + our trace analyzer:
```
NCCL op timeline (sample window):
- allreduce start (0us)
- chunk0 ring send  0-120us
- chunk0 ring recv 120-240us
- allreduce wait  240-800us  <-- long tail
- chunk1 tree gather 800-920us
- kernel streams idle 920-1600us

Note: when message size is ~48KB, ring phase finishes but we get a ~500us tail where slots blocked waiting on small kv-flushes + scheduler delay.
```

profiler-bot: auto-profile summary attached: p50 p90 allreduce: 0.6ms / 1.4ms at 48KB, 0.9ms / 2.7ms at 64KB, and 3.1ms / 6.2ms at 512KB. C/C++ stack shows repeated calls into our kv_cache flush path.

maria: interesting — our KV cache shards are emitting ~16 small updates per rank at that size (each 3KB-4KB) which we coalesce poorly. small updates cause repeated short all-reduces. could be message shape fragmentation forcing NCCL into less-efficient transfers.

devon_ops: is this the case where our batching heuristic lets KV flush interleave with optimizer comms? we currently flush kv on token boundary and don't coalesce across micro-batches.

alex_chiang: yes. timeline shows interleaved tiny allreduces from kv flushes that break up the big reduce, causing many extra syncs. trying a quick patch to coalesce kv updates across a small time window (config: kv.coalesce_ms=2).

samir: also try forcing NCCL algorithm to TREE for that message size to see if scheduling improves. env override: `NCCL_ALGO=tree` and `NCCL_MIN_NRINGS=0` for the run.

rita_khan: FYI tree helps with latency tails in our earlier microbenchmarks for medium msgs, ring wins for large contiguous payloads. kernel selection + NCCL topology interplay matters.

alex_chiang: ran 3 runs: baseline, kv-coalesce patch, kv-coalesce+NCCL_ALGO=tree. results (p90 allreduce):
- baseline: 1.4ms (48KB window)
- coalesce: 0.9ms (35% drop)
- coalesce + tree: 0.75ms (46% drop vs baseline)
But at 512KB, tree regresses (baseline 3.1ms -> coalesce+tree 4.2ms).

maria: expected. tree reduces scheduling stalls when many small messages interleave, but for big contiguous transfers ring has better bandwidth utilization. we need a policy that picks algo by message shape and current inflight fragmentation.

devon_ops: practical approach: detect message-size distribution per-step and set NCCL_ALGO dynamically or split large KV flushes to align with model allreduce windows. we could also tweak our kernel selection to prefer kernels that overlap better with comm when fragmentation present.

samir: can we adjust our batching heuristic instead? e.g., hold KV flushes up to X bytes or Y ms to merge into fewer larger allreduces. simpler than dynamic NCCL.

alex_chiang: proof-of-concept for coalesce window already shows good wins for medium msgs. downside: increases tail-latency variability for very low-latency workloads. need safe defaults + opt-out flag per-model.

rita_khan: add a kernel-selection rule: when coalesce_active and avg_msg_size < 128KB, prefer kernels that launch smaller compute chunks and yield earlier to network streams. that should improve overlap. can you sketch the config?

alex_chiang: sketch:
```json
{"runtime": {"kv_coalesce_ms": 2, "comm_policy": {"msg_size_thresholds": [65536, 524288], "algorithms": ["auto","tree","ring"]}, "kernel_hints": {"prefer_preemptible_kernels": true}}}
```

maria: one more datapoint: nvidia-driver shows PCIe retries bump during the cliff, maybe reordering created bursts. worth checking NIC/PCI congestion counters.

devon_ops: opened a small infra ticket to capture pcie counters and NIC queue depths next run. ticket #INF-3421.

samir: long-term: runtime should track real-time msg-size histogram (per-step) and pick both kernel and NCCL algo before the step starts. cheap classifier + a few microbenchmarks at startup should work. also add regression alert if p90 increases > 20% over baseline.

alex_chiang: agreed. i'll: 1) stabilize kv-coalesce patch with opt flags, 2) add lightweight msg-histogram and a simple selection heuristic, 3) instrument PCIe/NIC metrics. will post follow-ups. thanks all. :thumbsup:

rita_khan: nice work. once stable, run a small rollout on dedicated to validate (canary 5% traffic).

profiler-bot: note — attached aggregated traces for the 3 runs, saved under /prof/traces/2412345678/ for those who want to dig in.

alex_chiang: saved patch in PR #4123, will queue perf run at 03:00 UTC.
